data.title: The Origin of the Research University
data.author: Petiver
data.article_summary: 文章探讨了研究型大学的起源，特别是19世纪德国大学如何从以教学为主的中世纪机构转变为兼具教学与研究的现代大学模式。在此之前，大学并非新知识生产的主要场所，学术研究多在如英国皇家学会等机构进行。然而，19世纪的德国大学通过将研究纳入其体系，迅速成为知识生产的核心，推动了化学、物理学、细胞理论、细菌学和科学医学等领域的重大进展。这一变革不仅使德国大学主导了当时的学术界，还影响了整个欧洲乃至后来的美国大学体系。文章还讨论了为何这一变革发生在政治分裂、科学氛围薄弱的德国，以及这一历史对当今学术界面临的挑战有何启示。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：学术体系的历史、现状及其问题

不同观点：
• [bonoboTP] 认为19世纪前的许多重要知识分子并非在大学体系内工作，而现代学术界倾向于将自己塑造成知识的唯一传承者和开拓者。此外， peer review、影响因子等机制缺乏历史背景和替代方案的讨论，学生在学术体系中缺乏反思和元认知的机会。
• [megaloblasto] 对美国研究型大学感到失望，认为这些大学更关注研究影响而非本科教育质量。大学利用学生作为稳定收入来源，而教育质量却得不到保障，学生的利益受损。
• [djoldman] 通过分享圣学术节骚乱的历史事件，暗示过去的学生行为问题，反映出不同时期的大学文化和学生纪律问题。
• [ricksunny] 提到一位前MIT林肯实验室研究员的工作，强调19世纪中期至战前德国技术专家对科学和历史的贡献，提供了一个具体的历史参考。
• [dr_dshiv] 认为亚历山大港的Mouseion是研究型大学的起源，强调其在人文和科学方面的贡献，并持续了几百年，提供了一个古代学术机构的例子。
• [dlcarrier] 认为教育和学术应该分离，暗示当前的体系存在问题。
• [mistrial9] 对某些对学术历史的不严谨描述提出批评，认为一些概括性的陈述缺乏可信度，同时对学术资历和无意义出版物的问题提出见解。

补充讨论：
• 评论中涉及多个历史例子和资源链接，如圣学术节骚乱和德国技术专家的贡献，提供了具体的历史背景和参考资料。
• 争议的焦点包括学术体系的历史描述的可信度和现代学术机制（如peer review和影响因子）的讨论不足。
• 反思和元认知在学术教育中的重要性也被提出，强调学生对学术体系本身的理解和批判性思考能力。

总结：评论中主要讨论了学术体系的历史演变、现代大学教育的问题以及学术机制的反思。不同评论者从历史背景、个人经历和学术机制等角度提出了各自的观点和批评。争议点主要集中在历史描述的准确性和现代学术机制的合理性上。

44484409.article_content:
The Origin of the Research University
Clara Collier
Universities have existed for more than a thousand years — and for almost all of that time, they weren’t centers of research. What changed in 19th century Germany?
If you were alive in 1800 and someone asked you about the future of research, it wouldn’t occur to you to mention the university. Real scholarship happened in new, modern, enlightened institutions like the British Royal Society or the French
Académie des sciences.
Universities were a medieval relic. And nowhere was it more medieval, hidebound, and generally dysfunctional than in the German-speaking world.
But something happened to German universities at the turn of the 19th century — they developed a new system that combined teaching with research. Within a few decades, everyone in Europe was trying to copy their model. German scientists dominated chemistry and revolutionized modern physics. They came up with cell theory, bacteriology, the whole laboratory-based model of scientific medicine, and I don’t think it’s much of a stretch to say that they invented the social sciences in almost full generality. By the end of the century, they were the greatest engine of organized knowledge production the world had ever seen — and if they’ve since been surpassed by the American university system, that’s mostly because we copied them.
I think we don't properly appreciate how surprising this is. It’s odd that the research university exists at all. Universities have been around for a thousand years, but for most of their history, they were not seen as institutions for producing new knowledge. It’s even stranger that it came to be in a land which was politically fragmented, lacked a strong scientific community, and had very limited interest in creating one.
So I can’t help but ask: Why Germany? Why universities? Why does the entire modern institutional research ecosystem look the way it does? Does this history have anything to tell us about how to navigate an era of intense hostility and pessimism towards academia? (No promises!) Who made this thing? Were they even trying to? And why does it work so well?
Bibliotheca Büloviana Acaddemae, Georgiae Augustae donata Göttinga, engraved by Georg Daniel Heumann (1691–1759). Göttingen University Library, founded in 1734, was considered the first academic research library.
German universities in the age of Enlightenment
Scholars at early modern universities did research — but it was on their own time. Universities in early modern Europe were teaching institutions. Their primary purpose was to produce priests, lawyers, and doctors. To this end, they had four traditional faculties: theology, law, medicine, and what the Germans called philosophy.  This last included everything
that might be part of a modern arts and sciences education — any subject, from poetry to physics, which wasn’t directly pre-professional. Of the four, it  was by far the least prestigious and worst attended. Professors were paid exclusively for lecturing, usually not very much, and professors of the arts and sciences were paid the least of all.
Starting in the 16th century, these factors tended to push the people most interested in advancing human knowledge outside of universities. The trend started in astronomy. Copernicus, Brahe, and Galileo all began their careers as university professors, and all left for positions as civil servants or court astronomers which offered more money and more freedom. (Kepler, because of his heterodox approach to Lutheranism, was never able to secure a university chair at all.) Some universities tried to invest in experimental facilities — an observatory at Utrecht, a chemical laboratory at Altdorf — but these couldn’t compete with the great private or government-funded facilities being built in England and France. While many intellectuals stayed in academia, leading scholars were more and more likely to take up better offers elsewhere. The intellectual center of gravity shifted from universities to the international republic of letters.
German universities in the Age of Enlightenment shared all of these problems and more. Their curriculum was, quite literally, medieval. So were their endowments. Hiring was rife with nepotism — and even when it didn’t involve replacing a professor with someone’s son or son-in-law, it was loosely related to any modern conception of academic merit. Specialization was non-existent. It hardly mattered if a professor of oriental languages could read Hebrew or Arabic, so long as he had adequate seniority, and a poetry professor who wanted a raise might well be handed an additional chair in mathematics. The students were menaces, given to drunkenness, gambling, dueling, and chronically skipping class.
Everyone agreed that German universities needed to change. But very few people thought that this should involve making them centers of free intellectual inquiry. Instead, Enlightenment critics wanted them to be
useful
. A scholar of the 17th

data.title: Show HN: I built a playground to showcase what Flux Kontext is good at
data.author: Zephyrion
data.article_summary: Flux Kontext Dev是一款免费的在线AI图像编辑工具，无需注册，可即时使用。用户上传图片并描述所需修改，工具将自动完成编辑。它支持修改图像元素、照片修复与上色、照片风格转换、文字编辑、Logo增强、去除人群以及产品展示等多种功能。该工具基于FLUX.1 Kontext [dev]模型，拥有120亿参数，针对消费级硬件优化，并兼容多种推理框架。它提供开放权重，供研究和非商业使用，具有高性能和精确的编辑能力，是开源图像编辑技术的新标准。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Kontext模型的功能、可用性、技术问题及其实际效果的争议

不同观点：
• **vunderba的观点**：Kontext模型在图像编辑方面有革命性意义，能够对图像局部进行修改而不影响其他部分，节省了遮罩和修复的时间。他还提到该模型支持多图像合成，展示了其强大功能。
• **roenxi的观点**：虽然Kontext模型的发布被延迟，且未公开权重导致无法商用，但其在公众领域的出现仍是一个进步，超越了稳定扩散模型的简单提示词机制。
• **bsenftner的观点**：质疑提供公共访问的财务支持，怀疑背后是否有大型组织或资金支持，而非个人行为。
• **chrismorgan的观点**：对“AI精度”持怀疑态度，指出Kontext在图像修复和着色方面仍存在一些问题，如图像重构和现实性，并建议更严谨的修改前后对比。
• **merelysounds和fazza999、shekhar101的观点**：在使用Kontext时遇到错误信息，处理失败，对用户体验表示失望，并与其他工具（如MidJourney）进行对比。
• **winterrx和mg的观点**：关注Kontext模型的运行成本及服务器问题，好奇其免费服务的财务可持续性和技术实现方式。

补充讨论：
• **商业可用性**：roenxi指出Kontext模型未公开权重，限制了商业应用。
• **技术问题**：多个用户（merelysounds、fazza999、shekhar101）报告使用过程中遇到错误，影响使用体验。
• **功能展示与对比**：chrismorgan建议更严谨的对比方式以展示模型的修改效果。
• **财务与技术支持**：bsenftner、winterrx和mg关注模型提供免费访问的财务支持和运行方式。

data.title: Async Ruby Is the Future of AI Apps (and It's Already Here)
data.author: doppp
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了在Ruby中使用异步编程来处理大型语言模型（LLM）应用的优势。作者Carmine Paolino对比了Ruby和Python在异步编程上的发展，指出Ruby的异步模型在应对LLM应用的独特需求（如长时间连接和逐字响应）上更加高效。传统基于线程的并发模型（如SolidQueue、Sidekiq）在处理大量并发对话时面临资源浪费和性能瓶颈，而Ruby的异步模型通过Fibers实现了更好的资源利用和性能提升。文章详细分析了线程与异步在调度和管理资源上的区别，强调Ruby的异步模型无需重写代码即可提升性能，是应对现代AI应用挑战的理想选择。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于Ruby中异步编程的优缺点及性能讨论

不同观点：
• [horsawlarway] 认为该文章宣传的“无需回调、无需承诺、无需async/await关键字”具有讽刺意味，因为示例中仍出现了"async do"和"end.map(&:wait)"。他还指出，文章中关于每个worker需要一个数据库连接的论点可以通过pgbouncer等工具缓解。此外，他认为Ruby在处理长期运行的LLM聊天任务时并不是最佳选择，尤其在性能方面，Ruby并不是追求速度和效率的首选语言。
• [hakunin] 赞赏文章的清晰写作，并支持文章的观点，认为Ruby的异步编程允许直接使用“任何Ruby代码”，这与其他要求使用特定声明式函数或语法的库不同。他强调Ruby的这种特性使得开发者可以使用完整的Ruby功能，而不是受限于某种特定语法。
• [knowitnone] 指出，如果性能是主要考虑因素，那么选择脚本语言如Ruby并不是明智之举，因为即便是微秒级的延迟也会累积成实际的延迟。
• [moralestapia] 认为Python和Ruby开发者正在“发现”JavaScript十年前的标准做法，表现出一种对这种模仿行为的倦怠感，但也承认这是一种恭维形式。

补充讨论：
• [Alifatisk] 对Ruby异步编程的视角表示兴趣，并对I/O多路复用示例表示赞赏，显示出对技术细节的关注和认可。

争议焦点：

Async Ruby is the Future of AI Apps (And It's Already Here)
Carmine Paolino
Jul 9, 2025
After a decade as an ML engineer/scientist immersed in Python’s async ecosystem, returning to Ruby felt like stepping back in time. Where was the async revolution? Why was everyone still using threads for everything? SolidQueue, Sidekiq, GoodJob – all thread-based. Even newer solutions defaulted to the same concurrency model.
Coming from Python, where the entire community had reorganized around
asyncio
, this seemed bizarre. FastAPI replaced Flask. Every library spawned an async twin. The transformation was total and necessary.
Then, building
RubyLLM
and
Chat with Work
, I noticed that
LLM communication is async Ruby’s killer app
. The unique demands of streaming AI responses – long-lived connections, token-by-token delivery, thousands of concurrent conversations – expose exactly why async matters.
Here’s the exciting bit: once I understood Ruby’s approach to async, I realized it’s actually
superior
to Python’s. While Python forced everyone to rewrite their entire stack, Ruby quietly built something better. Your existing code just works. No syntax changes. No library migrations. Just better performance when you need it.
The async ecosystem that
Samuel Williams
and others have been building for years suddenly makes perfect sense. We just needed the right use case to see it.
Why LLM Communication Breaks Everything
LLM applications create a perfect storm of challenges that expose every weakness in thread-based concurrency:
1. Slot Starvation
Configure any thread-based job queue with 25 workers:
class
StreamAIResponseJob
<
ApplicationJob
def
perform
(
chat
,
message
)
# This job occupies 1 of your 25 slots...
chat
.
ask
(
message
)
do
|
chunk
|
# ...for the ENTIRE streaming duration (30-60 seconds)
broadcast_chunk
(
chunk
)
# Thread is 99% idle, just waiting for tokens
end
# Slot only freed here, after full response
end
end
Your 26th user? They’re waiting in line. Not because your server is busy, but because all your workers are occupied by jobs waiting for tokens.
2. Resource Multiplication
Each thread needs its own:
Database connection (25 threads = 25 connections minimum)
Stack memory allocation
OS thread management overhead
For 1000 concurrent conversations, you’d need 1000 threads. Each thread needs its database connection. That’s 1000 database connections for threads that are 99% idle.
3. Performance Overhead
Real benchmarks show
1
:
Creating a thread: ~80μs
Thread context switch: ~1.3μs
Maximum throughput: ~5,000 requests/second
When you’re handling thousands of streaming connections, these microseconds add up to real latency.
4. Scalability Challenges
Try creating 10,000 threads and the OS scheduler starts to struggle. The overhead becomes crushing. Yet modern AI apps need to handle thousands of concurrent conversations.
These aren’t separate issues – they’re all symptoms of the same architectural mismatch. LLM communication is fundamentally different from traditional background jobs.
Understanding Concurrency: Threads vs Async
To understand why LLM applications are async’s perfect use case – and why Ruby’s implementation is so elegant – we need to build up from first principles.
The Hierarchy: Processes, Threads, and Fibers
Think of your computer as an office building:
Processes
are like separate offices – each with its own locked door, furniture, and files. They can’t see into each other’s spaces (memory isolation).
Threads
are like workers sharing the same office – they can access the same filing cabinets (shared memory) but need to coordinate to avoid collisions.
Fibers
are like multiple tasks juggled by one worker at their desk – switching between them manually when waiting for something (like a phone call).
Scheduling: The Core Difference
The fundamental question in concurrency is: who decides when to switch between tasks?
Threads: Preemptive Multitasking
With threads, the operating system is the boss. It forcibly interrupts running threads to give others a turn:

# Each thread blocks individually here

)
end
end
Each thread:
Gets scheduled by the OS kernel
Can be interrupted mid-execution (in Ruby, after 100ms)
Blocks individually on I/O operations
Requires OS resources and kernel data structures
Needs its own resources (like database connections)
Fibers: Cooperative Concurrency
With fibers, switching is voluntary – they only yield at I/O boundaries:

Fixing underground water pipes usually means digging up roads and sidewalks — a process that's disruptive and expensive. However, researchers at the University of Sheffield in the U.K. are working on a different approach. They've developed small robots called "Pipebots" that can travel inside water pipes to find and potentially repair leaks, all without any excavation.
Sign up for my FREE CyberGuy Report
Get my best tech tips, urgent security alerts, and exclusive deals delivered straight to your inbox. Plus, you’ll get instant access to my Ultimate Scam Survival Guide — free when you join my
CYBERGUY.COM/NEWSLETTER.
Pipebot in various environments.
(University of Sheffield)
Old leaky underground pipes are causing a crisis
The U.K. has some of the oldest water systems in the world, with parts of the network still dating back to the Victorian era. Not surprisingly, many of these pipes are leaking, wasting about 790 million gallons of water every day. Fixing them usually means digging up streets, which causes major disruption and adds to the country's $5 billion a year maintenance costs.
A prototype of a Pipebot.
(University of Sheffield)
Little robots come to the rescue
Pipebots are tiny, high-tech helpers designed to navigate the underground world of water pipes. Each one comes with acoustic sensors, cameras, and rugged wheels that help it move through tight, twisty spaces-while smart enough to steer clear of off-limits areas.
They're dropped into the water system through hydrants and travel in groups, scanning the inside of pipes for even the smallest cracks. When they spot a problem, they send the details back to engineers above ground, making it easier to fix issues without digging anything up.
An illustration showing that a Pipebot has found a leak.
(University of Sheffield)
The robots are part of a bigger innovation plan
These robots are part of a larger effort to modernize how the U.K. manages its aging water infrastructure. The initiative isn't just a university research project-it's supported by the U.K.'s water regulator, OFWAT (the Water Services Regulation Authority), and involves several collaborative projects.
One of these projects focuses on using Pipebots to inspect live, pressurized wastewater pipes, also known as raising mains. The goal is to catch problems early and make repairs before leaks cause pollution.
Another project, called "no dig leak repair," is working on ways to fix leaks from inside the water mains themselves, completely avoiding the need for disruptive roadwork.
There's also the EU-funded Pipeon Project, which is developing advanced, AI-powered robots that can inspect sewers autonomously, without human guidance.
Image of a Pipebot.
(University of Sheffield)
Kurt's key takeaways
These little robots could be exactly what countries everywhere need to keep their water systems running smoothly. They have the potential to make maintenance cleaner, more affordable, and way more efficient. That's especially important for developing countries where budgets are tight and infrastructure is aging or incomplete. As the pressure to conserve water grows, tools like Pipebots could make a real difference in helping us manage this vital resource more wisely.

主要讨论点：Flix 语言的特性、优点、缺点以及与其他语言和生态系统（如JVM、Haskell、Scala等）的比较。

不同观点：
• **Flix 的优点和独特性**：exceptione 对 Flix 语言的代数数据类型、逻辑编程、可变性等特性印象深刻，尤其赞赏其单个可执行文件集成了包管理器、语言服务器协议（LSP）和编译器。他还提到 Flix 在与 JVM 生态系统（如 Java）集成方面的潜力，尽管存在类型擦除问题，但通过 "regions" 概念支持命令式交互。

• **记录的多态性语义**：Joker_vD 关注 Flix 的记录扩展和限制的多态性语义，认为其遵循 Leijen 的方法，允许记录字段的重加和移除，且行为合理。相比之下，早期尝试通过复杂的类型系统静态禁止这种行为显得不必要。

• **语法问题**：daxfohl 对 Flix 语法中的分号使用提出批评，特别是在 `yield` 示例中，最后一行没有 "return" 导致不对称感。他表示可以接受大括号或缩进，但分号必须去掉。

• **Flix 与 Java 的比较和教学**：lutzh 提到曾写过一篇 "Flix for Java Programmers" 的文章，认为 Flix 对于 Java 程序员来说非常有趣，但需要更新以反映 Flix 的最新发展。

• **Aarhus 作为编程语言研究重镇的原因**：textlapse 提出一个题外问题，探讨丹麦奥胡斯大学/科技中心为何成为编程语言研究的强大中心，涉及 C++、C#、Typescript、Dart 等语言的根源。

• **类型类和宏的支持**：pshirshov 关注 Flix 是否支持高阶类型（HKTs）和类型类（在 Flix 中称为 traits）。他对缺乏标称继承表示失望，认为这使得某些有用的抽象无法实现或变得丑陋。

• **代码智能工具的支持**：daxfohl 幽默地提到，是否需要依赖代码智能工具，还是需要自己动脑。同时担心 LLMs 可能会抑制新语言的采用。

• **对 Flix 的兴趣和使用意愿**：andoando 表达了对 Flix 的喜爱，这是他第一次看到新编程语言演示后产生使用欲望。voat 则表示尽管 Flix 看起来很美，但自己是 Web 开发者，从不接触 JVM 生态系统。

• **效果导向编程的介绍需求**：mcdow 请求关于效果导向编程的具体介绍和使用示例。

• **与其他语言的比较**：syhol 指出 Flix 与 Koka 语言非常相似，并希望这些效果系统能够成为主流。Hashex129542 则简单地表示不喜欢过多的关键字。

• **模式匹配的语法建议**：pmontra 对比了 Flix 和 Elixir 的模式匹配语法，建议 Flix 可以更简洁、更 DRY（不重复自己），并提出结构化模式匹配的概念。

• **查询语法的顺序问题**：naasking 对 Flix 查询语句中 `select` 的位置提出异议，认为应该像 LINQ 那样将 `select` 放在最后，以避免 SQL 中的问题。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及的 Flix 文档和外部资源链接（如 lutzh 的文章、Flix 官方文档中的 JVM 互操作性说明）为深入了解 Flix 提供了参考。

主要讨论点：Flix 语言的特性、优点、缺点以及与其他语言和生态系统（如JVM、Haskell、Scala等）的比较。

不同观点：
• **Flix 的优点和独特性**：exceptione 对 Flix 语言的代数数据类型、逻辑编程、可变性等特性印象深刻，尤其赞赏其单个可执行文件集成了包管理器、语言服务器协议（LSP）和编译器。他还提到 Flix 在与 JVM 生态系统（如 Java）集成方面的潜力，尽管存在类型擦除问题，但通过 "regions" 概念支持命令式交互。

• **记录的多态性语义**：Joker_vD 关注 Flix 的记录扩展和限制的多态性语义，认为其遵循 Leijen 的方法，允许记录字段的重加和移除，且行为合理。相比之下，早期尝试通过复杂的类型系统静态禁止这种行为显得不必要。

• **语法问题**：daxfohl 对 Flix 语法中的分号使用提出批评，特别是在 `yield` 示例中，最后一行没有 "return" 导致不对称感。他表示可以接受大括号或缩进，但分号必须去掉。

• **Flix 与 Java 的比较和教学**：lutzh 提到曾写过一篇 "Flix for Java Programmers" 的文章，认为 Flix 对于 Java 程序员来说非常有趣，但需要更新以反映 Flix 的最新发展。

• **Aarhus 作为编程语言研究重镇的原因**：textlapse 提出一个题外问题，探讨丹麦奥胡斯大学/科技中心为何成为编程语言研究的强大中心，涉及 C++、C#、Typescript、Dart 等语言的根源。

• **类型类和宏的支持**：pshirshov 关注 Flix 是否支持高阶类型（HKTs）和类型类（在 Flix 中称为 traits）。他对缺乏标称继承表示失望，认为这使得某些有用的抽象无法实现或变得丑陋。

• **代码智能工具的支持**：daxfohl 幽默地提到，是否需要依赖代码智能工具，还是需要自己动脑。同时担心 LLMs 可能会抑制新语言的采用。

• **对 Flix 的兴趣和使用意愿**：andoando 表达了对 Flix 的喜爱，这是他第一次看到新编程语言演示后产生使用欲望。voat 则表示尽管 Flix 看起来很美，但自己是 Web 开发者，从不接触 JVM 生态系统。

• **效果导向编程的介绍需求**：mcdow 请求关于效果导向编程的具体介绍和使用示例。

• **与其他语言的比较**：syhol 指出 Flix 与 Koka 语言非常相似，并希望这些效果系统能够成为主流。Hashex129542 则简单地表示不喜欢过多的关键字。

• **模式匹配的语法建议**：pmontra 对比了 Flix 和 Elixir 的模式匹配语法，建议 Flix 可以更简洁、更 DRY（不重复自己），并提出结构化模式匹配的概念。

• **查询语法的顺序问题**：naasking 对 Flix 查询语句中 `select` 的位置提出异议，认为应该像 LINQ 那样将 `select` 放在最后，以避免 SQL 中的问题。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及的 Flix 文档和外部资源链接（如 lutzh 的文章、Flix 官方文档中的 JVM 互操作性说明）为深入了解 Flix 提供了参考。

data.author: akyshnik
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：语音AI在客户支持中的应用及其实际效果

不同观点：
• joshribakoff: 认为当前的语音AI无法有效区分背景噪音和用户的回应，且无法处理非选择题形式的用户问题。用户假装不说英语或发出奇怪声音时，才能更快接入人工客服，说明AI不够智能。
• mandeepj: 提出可以通过使用已录制的客户支持电话进行AI训练，以改善AI的表现，并建议持续监测和调整AI的表现。
• devonsolomon: 强调用户打电话通常是为了与人类交流，而非AI。如果AI无法提供比网站更好的服务，用户会感到沮丧。AI更适合用于其他特定场景，而非完全取代呼叫中心。
• AndrewKemendo: 认为语音AI可以作为个人电话管理的选项，并描述了一个自我改进的个人语音AI模型，但强调不会分享个人数据。
• ljclifford: 对语音AI在客户支持领域的潜力表示乐观，并表示愿意合作，期待看到更多的进展。
• joelthelion: 质疑为何 demo 中没有展示实际通话，认为这才能更具说服力。
• froh42: 亲身体验到语音AI的误解问题，认为这种技术目前还不够成熟，不适合用于商业用途。
• costcopizza: 关注语音AI可能导致的就业岗位减少问题。
• ajeet: 祝贺发布并同意A/B测试和持续改进的重要性，但指出从测试中得出正确结论更具挑战性。
• ookblah: 对demo印象深刻，但感觉与AI交流时需要特别注意措辞，且AI的回应过于“ polished”，感觉不够真实。
• hajrice: 希望能够直接注册而不是请求demo，并对网站的“请求demo”按钮功能提出质疑。
• isabelleilyia: 关注语音AI在法律等敏感领域的应用，询问成功率和参与时间。
• cootsnuck: 关心语音AI的扩展性，询问单个语音代理能同时处理多少通电话。
• koakuma-chan: 比较语音AI与livekit，并询问文档问题。
• shahahmed: 祝贺发布并询问评估管理的方式。

补充讨论：
• 语音AI的实际效果和用户体验是争议的焦点，尤其是其在处理复杂问题和背景噪音方面的能力。
• 持续训练和改进语音AI的重要性被多次提及，包括使用真实客户数据进行训练和A/B测试。
• 用户对语音AI取代人工客服的接受度低，尤其是在敏感或复杂的使用场景中。
• 技术实现和扩展性也是讨论的重要方面，包括同时处理通话的能力和与现有技术的比较。

data.article_summary: 这篇文章主要介绍了ACT 2018应用范畴理论研究学校的开放申请信息，并提及了数理科学与几何学的相互联系。文章还概述了一系列关于图解线性代数的博客内容，包括各集主题和研究方向，并邀请读者订阅以获取更新。此外，文章还宣传了对博士生的需求，并提供了其他翻译资源和相关讨论。文章最后列出了一些历史博客条目和其他活动信息。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：图形化表示和简化语言在技术文档中的使用及其效果

不同观点：
• webprofusion认为文档中频繁使用“容易”和“简单”这样的词汇可能会让感到困惑的读者更加沮丧，尤其是当他们还没有理解相关概念时。使用这样的语言可能会适得其反，让读者感到更加无助。此外，作者强调永远不应该在解释文档中使用“显然”这样的词汇，因为如果事情真的显然，读者就不需要阅读解释了。

• AntonioL提到这让他想起牛津大学的Bob Coecke的工作，他提出了量子过程的图形化语言。这表明此类图形化表示在其他学术领域也有应用，并且可能受到先前研究的启发。

• marvinborner指出这些图形与使用对称交互组合子的交互网络中的计算编码有相似之处，并通过lambda演算的例子进行了说明。这表明图形化表示在不同计算理论中具有普遍性和一致性。

• theZilber分享了自己的学习体验，起初认为作者对简单概念的解释过于冗长，但后来意识到这种图形化表示帮助他更好地记住了数学概念及其名称。这表明图形化表示在教育中可能非常有效。

• dtj1123提到这让他想起zx-calculus，这表明zx-calculus和文中的图形化表示可能有相似之处，并且在量子计算等领域有应用。

• Xmd5a讨论了广义Transformer模型，这些模型可以操作函数、图形、概率分布等结构，而不仅限于矩阵和向量。这表明图形化表示在机器学习领域也有应用和探索。

• MarkusQ表示曾经和学生一起关注过这类工作，但感到遗憾的是这项工作似乎已经被放弃。这反映了某些学术研究可能因为各种原因未能持续下去。

• dclowd9901通过引用网络漫画，幽默地指出了人类在匿名情况下的行为倾向，这虽然不是直接讨论技术内容，但反映了网络文化中的某些现象。

• phforms分享了自己多年前阅读相关内容的体验，虽然只读了几章，但这些图形化表示在形式推理中的应用让他大开眼界。这表明图形化表示在学术研究中有启发性和趣味性。

• vismit2000提供了有关沉浸式线性代数的书籍链接，这为读者提供了进一步阅读和探索的资源。

• programjames指出文中的图形化表示与交互组合子有相似之处，并提供了相关链接，这为进一步研究提供了参考。

• lorenzo_medici的评论看似与主题无关，可能是幽默或个人观点的表达。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于使用“容易”和“简单”这样的词汇是否有助于读者理解。webprofusion认为这种语言可能让困惑的读者感到更加沮丧，而theZilber则认为这种图形化表示帮助他更好地理解和记忆数学概念。

• 不同评论提到了多种相关的学术领域和工具，如量子过程的图形化语言、lambda演算、zx-calculus、交互网络和广义Transformer模型，这表明图形化表示在多个领域有应用和探索。

• 一些评论反映了个人学习体验和感受，如theZilber和phforms，他们认为图形化表示在教育中非常有效，并能激发学习兴趣。

• 某些评论提到了相关工作的持续性和发展情况，如MarkusQ提到的工作可能已经被放弃，这反映了学术研究中的一些现实问题。

• 一些评论反映了个人学习体验和感受，如theZilber和phforms，他们认为图形化表示在教育中非常有效，并能激发学习兴趣。

• 某些评论提到了相关工作的持续性和发展情况，如MarkusQ提到的工作可能已经被放弃，这反映了学术研究中的一些现实问题。

data.title: Retail cyber attacks: NCA arrest four for attacks on M&S, Co-op and Harrods
data.author: sandwichsphinx
data.article_summary: 英国国家犯罪局（NCA）逮捕了四名涉嫌参与网络攻击的人员，目标包括M&S、Co-op和Harrods等大型零售商。两名19岁男性、一名17岁男性和一名20岁女性在西米德兰兹和伦敦被捕，涉嫌违反《计算机滥用法》、敲诈、洗钱及参与有组织犯罪。所有被捕者的电子设备已被扣押进行数字取证分析。NCA表示，调查仍在继续，将与国内外合作伙伴合作，确保将责任人绳之以法。此次行动得到了西米德兰兹地区有组织犯罪部门和东米德兰兹特别行动部门的支持。受害者应通过政府的网络事件指引网站报告类似事件。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对青少年黑客行为及公司网络安全问题的讨论

不同观点：
• **公司安全疏忽是主要问题**：[cedws] 认为，尽管事件聚焦在青少年黑客上，但根本问题是公司方面的安全疏忽。
• **系统复杂性导致恢复困难**：[djaychela] 通过其在公司高管朋友的经历说明，现代零售企业的系统高度互联，遭遇网络攻击后恢复正常运作非常困难，给管理层带来巨大压力。
• **黑客年龄引发的感慨**：[gluten_guardian] 对年轻黑客的年龄表示惊讶，认为与自己年轻时的行为相比，现代青少年的犯罪行为更加复杂，并表示希望了解更多关于攻击类型的细节。
• **黑客地域性引发的质疑**：[clort] 对嫌疑人位于英国表示意外，似乎暗示对嫌疑人地域的怀疑。
• **攻击手段的技术细节**：[lyu07282] 提供了具体的技术细节，指出黑客通过伪装成员工并利用帮助台重置密码，进而控制系统并实施勒索，引用了相关技术文章作为来源。
• **访问受限引发的不满**：[casenmgreen] 提到因使用Tor网络导致无法访问相关网站，表达了不满。
• **系统漏洞的责任归属**：[devwastaken] 持激进观点，认为根本不存在“网络犯罪”，问题在于系统设计缺陷。主张要求科技公司对漏洞负责，并提出应由持证工程师开发软件，反对外包和廉价劳动力。
• **怀疑有外部支持**：[aaronrobinson] 怀疑此次攻击背后有外国势力支持，认为仅凭社会工程学难以完成如此复杂的攻击，暗示可能有更大规模的组织参与。

补充讨论：
• **关于攻击手段和责任归属的争议**：评论中既有对黑客具体攻击手段的讨论（如[lyu07282]），也有对系统漏洞责任的激进观点（如[devwastaken]），反映出对网络安全事件中责任归属的不同看法。
• **地域和外部支持的质疑**：[clort] 和 [aaronrobinson] 对黑客的地域和潜在外部支持表示怀疑，反映出对国际网络犯罪复杂性的关注。

News
Retail cyber attacks: NCA arrest four for attacks on M&S, Co-op and Harrods
Expired
Cybercrime
Four people have been arrested in the UK as part of a National Crime Agency investigation into cyber attacks targeting M&S, Co-op and Harrods.
Two males aged 19, another aged 17, and a 20-year-old female were apprehended in the West Midlands and London this morning (10 July) on suspicion of Computer Misuse Act offences, blackmail, money laundering and participating in the activities of an organised crime group.
All four were arrested at their home addresses and had their electronic devices seized for digital forensic analysis.
They remain in custody for questioning by officers from the NCA's National Cyber Crime Unit in relation to the three attacks, which took place in April this year.
Deputy Director Paul Foster, head of the NCA's National Cyber Crime Unit, said:
"Since these attacks took place, specialist NCA cybercrime investigators have been working at pace and the investigation remains one of the Agency's highest priorities.
"Today's arrests are a significant step in that investigation but our work continues, alongside partners in the UK and overseas, to ensure those responsible are identified and brought to justice.
"Cyber attacks can be hugely disruptive for businesses and I'd like to thank M&S, Co-op and Harrods for their support to our investigations. Hopefully this signals to future victims the importance of seeking support and engaging with law enforcement as part of the reporting process. The NCA and policing are here to help."
Today's operational activity was supported by officers from the West Midlands Regional Organised Crime Unit and the East Midlands Special Operations Unit.
Victims of cybercrime should use the Government's
Cyber Incident Signposting Site
for direction on which agencies to report an incident to.

data.title: Red Hat Technical Writing Style Guide
data.author: jumpocelot
data.article_summary: 《Red Hat 技术写作风格指南》是红帽公司内部多个团队合作的成果，旨在为技术文档提供写作规范和词语使用建议。该指南涵盖语法（如主动语态、一致性、标点符号使用等）、设计（如标题、界面文档、字体使用）、语言选择（如避免误导性语言、使用包容性语言）、以及如何有效使用交叉引用等内容。此外，指南还包含一个词语使用词典，为技术写作中常见的词汇提供正确用法示例。该文档依据Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported许可证发布，使用时需注明出处并遵循相关商标规定。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：技术写作指南的各个方面，包括其质量、内容准确性、语法问题以及与其他风格指南的比较。

不同观点：
• jonathanlydall认为好的技术写作类似于好的室内设计，只有当写作不好时才会被注意到。好的技术文档应该让读者轻松获取信息，而不被写作本身的问题所干扰。
• azangru对指南中关于连贯句子的例子提出质疑，认为初始版本并非连贯句子，添加逗号只是语调需要，而非语法错误。
• kaycebasques指出技术写作指南常混淆“最佳实践”和“惯例”，前者有实验数据或共识支持，后者仅为保持一致性，建议在讨论时应明确区分。
• hliyana赞赏指南对商业术语的批评，强调语言应明确具体，避免无数据支持的超级形容词和不必要的术语。
• AdmiralAsshat认为指南中混合了基础语法规则和最佳实践，基础语法规则对技术写作人员来说应是基本常识，无需特别说明。
• freedomben对指南的广度和清晰度表示赞赏，认为其对广泛人群有帮助，而不仅限于特定公司员工。
• latexr对指南中关于正确使用语言的部分感到奇怪，质疑是否因常见错误才需要明确规定。
• perching_aix作为英语非母语者，对指南中的例句表示不满，认为某些句子结构和用词不自然。
• jasoneckert幽默地表示对版权声明未使用“Copyleft”一词感到失望。
• phendrenad2询问该指南是否与IBM技术写作指南冲突，并提供链接供参考。
• dctoedt部分赞同指南，但指出某些改进建议可能会丢失原句中的重要隐含信息，对某些读者而言可能有影响。
• dghf质疑指南中关于代词使用的例子，认为应使用“whoever”而非“whomever”。
• dandano认为指南很扎实，并将其加入自己的参考列表，同时也参考其他写作系统如澳大利亚风格手册和Divio文档系统。
• markedathome询问该指南与其他知名公司如IBM、DEC、Sun、Apple、Microsoft等风格指南的比较，指出这些公司均有内部印刷厂和风格指南。
• GLdRH认为指南的某些部分（如4.6节）很荒谬，但可以选择忽略。

补充讨论：
• 技术写作指南中“最佳实践”和“惯例”的区分是重要讨论点，影响指南的实用性和讨论效率。
• 对指南中例句和语法建议的准确性存在争议，特别是英语非母语者的观点。
• 对基础语法规则是否应在技术写作指南中明确规定存在不同看法。
• 对商业术语和超级形容词的批评获得一定认同，强调语言的具体和明确性。
• 与其他知名公司技术写作指南的比较也引起关注，反映出行业内对一致性和实用性的关注。

asyncmcp - Async transport layers for MCP
Overview
A regular MCP Server but working over queues :
queue-based-mcp-example.mov
Quoting from the
official description
:
MCP is an open protocol that standardizes how applications provide context to LLMs.
But a lot of this context is not always readily available and takes time for the applications to process - think batch processing APIs, webhooks or queues. In these cases with the current transport layers, the MCP server would have to expose a light-weight polling wrapper in the MCP layer to allow waiting and polling for the tasks to be done. Although SSE does provide async functionalities but it comes with caveats.
asyncmcp explores supporting more of the async transport layer implementations for MCP clients and servers, beyond the officially supported stdio and Streamable Http transports.
The whole idea of an
MCP server with async transport layer
is that it doesn't have to respond immediately to any requests. It can choose to direct them to internal queues for processing and the client doesn't have to stick around for the response.
Current capabilities
Transport layer : sns-sqs
Server : Transport layer that listens to a queue for MCP requests and writes the responses to a topic
Client : Transport layer that writes requests to a topic and listens to a queue for responses
Installation and Usage
#
Using uv (recommended)
uv add asyncmcp
#
Using pip
pip install asyncmcp
Basic server setup
Note : we don't support FastMCP yet. The examples in this repo uses the
basic way of creating MCP servers and client

: For SQS - message size limits are applicable (256KB standard, 2MB extended)
Response Handling
: Async nature means responses may not be immediate

data.title: FOKS: Federated Open Key Service
data.author: ubj
data.article_summary: FOKS（Federated Open Key Service）是一个提供端到端后量子加密的Git托管服务，数据在本地加密后再上传至服务器，确保数据安全。它支持联邦制，用户可以选择自建或托管服务器，并通过现代后量子公钥加密技术防止量子计算攻击。FOKS还提供加密的键值存储，支持存储短字符串或大文件。其团队管理系统允许创建复杂团队结构，支持跨联邦服务器共享加密数据。设备管理功能支持YubiKey，并可在设备丢失时撤销其访问权限。FOKS通过简单的密钥层次结构实现这些功能，使用签名链和Merkle树确保安全性和防篡改。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：FOKS系统的设计、功能、潜在应用及其局限性

不同观点：
• **支持与期望**：[maxtaco] 作为FOKS的作者，强调了在2025年进行基本加密操作仍需大量“粘合”工作，并介绍了FOKS的设计目标，即提供一个开放系统，允许任意应用在其上构建，而无需依赖商业服务。此外，[WhatIsDukkha] 提到FOKS类似于Keybase的开源版本，并提供了相关博客链接。[marcopolo] 对FOKS的Git支持表示赞赏，认为这使得从Keybase迁移变得简单。

• **与现有工具的比较**：[TheCraiggers] 认为FOKS可以为密码管理工具pass提供更好的后端支持，特别是在管理和使用YubiKeys方面。[hobofan] 则表示，目前的SOPS工具已经能满足其大部分需求，且复杂度较低，因此对引入FOKS持保留态度。

• **团队协作与技术细节**：[pmw] 希望了解FOKS在团队协作方面的具体实现，并提出了两个比较：1) 与基于SSH的Linux共享机器的比较；2) 与去中心化的Radicle服务的比较。此外，[singpolyma3] 对FOKS的“联邦”机制表示关注，询问是否通过单一服务器实现团队数据存储和轻量级SSO。[iovoid] 则指出，FOKS要求所有管理员必须在同一主服务器上，这可能是一个重大限制。

• **密钥管理和安全性**：[raphinou] 提到在开放源项目中遇到的用户密钥更新、撤销和公钥分发问题，并询问FOKS是否能提供帮助。[akoboldfrying] 对FOKS的密钥层次结构表示困惑，特别是对基础密钥和用户密钥的加密、解密过程以及密钥轮换的实际操作方式提出疑问。

• **系统命名与界面设计**：[xtajv] 对FOKS的名称提出异议，认为容易被误解为不雅词汇，建议更名以增加项目接受度。[hofrogs] 则对FOKS主页上的AI生成图像表示不满，认为这会降低项目的可信度。

补充讨论：
• **存储与效率问题**：[aitchnyu] 关心FOKS在分支管理、增量备份、存储效率和数据同步方面的具体实现，特别是对于E2EE存储的有效性和便捷性提出期望。

• **用户体验与技术复杂性**：[soundofvictory] 对项目本身表示兴趣，但对主页上的图像设计提出批评。[akoboldfrying] 对密钥层次结构的复杂性表示关注，并希望进一步了解密钥轮换的具体操作及其对数据处理的影响。

总的来说，讨论主要围绕FOKS的功能、技术实现、团队协作支持及其潜在问题展开，参与者对FOKS的创新性表示认可，但也对其复杂性和命名等问题提出了改进建议。

44520419.article_content:
FOKS
the Federated Open Key Service (in beta)
What Can FOKS Do For Me?
$
foks
git create secrets
Created: foks://acme.co/alice/secrets
$
git
remote add origin foks://acme.co/alice/secrets
$
git
push origin main
⏻ Initializing FOKS ... ✅ done
️☝ ️Indexing packfiles ... ✅ done
️⬆️ Pushing objects to remote ... ✅ done
To foks://acme.co/alice/secrets
* [new branch]      main -> main
End-to-End Post-Quantum Encrypted Git Hosting
FOKS provides a secure, end-to-end encrypted Git hosting service.
Your data is encrypted on your machine before it is sent to the server,
and the server never sees data or filenames in unencrypted form.
This means that even if the server is compromised, your data is safe.
FOKS is federated, so the git server can be one that
you host, or one that is hosted for you.
Additionally, FOKS uses modern PQ-secure public-key cryptography, so all end-to-end
encrypted data is safe from quantum attacks.
$
foks
kv put /secrets/vitals/ssn 123-45-6789
$
foks
kv get /secrets/vitals/ssn -
123-45-6789
$
foks
kv put -f /secrets/doc.pdf ~/doc.pdf
$
foks
kv get /secrets/doc.pdf /tmp/doc.pdf
$
diff
~/doc.pdf /tmp/doc.pdf && echo "the same"
the same
End-to-End Post-Quantum Encrypted Key-Value Store
Internally, FOKS implements git atop an encrypted key-value store.
Clients encrypt keys and values before sending them up to the server,
and decrypt them upon retrieval. You can access
this key-value store directly, which can store either
short strings, or large data files.
$
foks
team list-memberships
owner    devops
member
[email protected]
member
[email protected]
(via
[email protected]
)
$
foks
team list devops
owner    alice
admin    bob
member
[email protected]
member   t:
[email protected]
Federated and Generalized Team Management
FOKS provides a federated and generalized team management system.
You can create teams, add members, and assign roles.
You can also delegate team management to other team members.
Teams can be members of other teams, allowing for complex
team topologies that can mirror real-world organizations.
Morever, teams can cross federated boundaries, allowing
users on different FOKS servers to share data with end-to-end encryption.
$
foks
key list
* laptop 2024-05-04    computer      active
neither 3213         backup        active
YubiKey 5 NFC        yubikey       active
desktop 2023-04-01   computer      revoked
Device Management with Full YubiKey Support
FOKS provides a device management system with full YubiKey support.
You can register your devices with FOKS and manage their access.
You can also revoke access to a device if it is lost or stolen.
Revoking triggers a cascading key-rotation across all teams you are members of,
whether local or federated. This keeps data secure going forward.
How Does It Work?
A Simple Key Hierarchy
To power applications like the Git and KV-Store shown above,
FOKS needs a shared symmetric key for all readers and writers
of the data, available only to the authorized devices, teams
users and keys that the authors specify. FOKS achieves
this natural application requirement with a simple key hierarchy.
Everything starts with base-level keys, like user device keys,
backup keys, or YubiKeys.
Device keys are generated on user devices
and never leave the machine they are generated on. They are protected
locally with system-specific encrypted stores where possible,
and passwords where not. Other base-level keys include backup keys
(for which a human-readable code is the seed), or YubiKeys.
Every user of the system has a sequence of per-user-keys (PUKs)
at the next level up the hierarchy. The secrets seeds for these keys are encrypted
for all available base-level keys. A PUK rotates whenever
a base-level key is removed.
At the next level up there are teams, which work much like users.
All members of the teams share per-team-keys (PTKs), which
are encrypted for the team's members, be they users (via PUKs)
or teams (via recursive PTKs).
Signature Chains
In FOKS, there are two types of
parties
: users and teams.
In both cases, there is a rotating list of constituents (be they
devices or team members), and as these constituents change, so
to does the corresponding active PUK or PTK. As such users and teams
share much protocol design and implementation mechanism.
In both cases, the set of keys that can sign on behalf of
the party changes over time, and it's crucial for security that
there is a careful accounting of these keys that resists
tampering by the FOKS server.
To prevent tampering, FOKS uses "signatures chains", a linear
chain of signatures that can be played back to verify
the ordering of signatures, and that each signature was performed
with a key that was valid at the time of signing.
Merkle Trees
When different parties or computers access keys for a party,
they do so via signature chains; they grab these chains from
the server and play them back to discover the current set of
keys that represent a party.
A compromised server can still cheat here by forking chai

• **团队协作与技术细节**：[pmw] 希望了解FOKS在团队协作方面的具体实现，并提出了两个比较：1) 与基于SSH的Linux共享机器的比较；2) 与去中心化的Radicle服务的比较。此外，[singpolyma3] 对FOKS的“联邦”机制表示关注，询问是否通过单一服务器实现团队数据存储和轻量级SSO。[iovoid] 则指出，FOKS要求所有管理员必须在同一主服务器上，这可能是一个重大限制。

• **密钥管理和安全性**：[raphinou] 提到在开放源项目中遇到的用户密钥更新、撤销和公钥分发问题，并询问FOKS是否能提供帮助。[akoboldfrying] 对FOKS的密钥层次结构表示困惑，特别是对基础密钥和用户密钥的加密、解密过程以及密钥轮换的实际操作方式提出疑问。

• **系统命名与界面设计**：[xtajv] 对FOKS的名称提出异议，认为容易被误解为不雅词汇，建议更名以增加项目接受度。[hofrogs] 则对FOKS主页上的AI生成图像表示不满，认为这会降低项目的可信度。

补充讨论：
• **存储与效率问题**：[aitchnyu] 关心FOKS在分支管理、增量备份、存储效率和数据同步方面的具体实现，特别是对于E2EE存储的有效性和便捷性提出期望。

• **用户体验与技术复杂性**：[soundofvictory] 对项目本身表示兴趣，但对主页上的图像设计提出批评。[akoboldfrying] 对密钥层次结构的复杂性表示关注，并希望进一步了解密钥轮换的具体操作及其对数据处理的影响。

总的来说，讨论主要围绕FOKS的功能、技术实现、团队协作支持及其潜在问题展开，参与者对FOKS的创新性表示认可，但也对其复杂性和命名等问题提出了改进建议。

data.author: gniting
data.article_summary: Perplexity推出了其首款AI驱动的网页浏览器Comet，旨在挑战Google Search，直接吸引用户。Comet initially仅对订阅其200美元月费的Max计划用户和候补名单上的部分邀请用户开放。该浏览器内置Perplexity的AI搜索引擎，默认提供AI生成的搜索结果摘要，并引入Comet Assistant，一个可自动化常规任务的AI助手，如总结邮件、管理标签和网页导航。用户可以通过侧边栏调用Comet Assistant，它能查看网页内容并回答相关问题。尽管市场竞争激烈，Perplexity CEO Srinivas希望Comet能成为用户默认浏览器，从而大幅增加用户请求。尽管AI浏览器是新兴领域，Google等巨头也在朝此方向发展，但Perplexity的早期数据表现良好，显示出一定的潜力。然而，说服用户更换浏览器可能比让他们放弃Google Search更难。

Perplexity on Wednesday launched its first
AI-powered web browser, called Comet
, marking the startup’s latest effort to challenge Google Search as the primary avenue people use to find information online.
At launch,
Comet
will be available first to subscribers of Perplexity’s $200-per-month Max plan, as well as a small group of invitees that signed up to a waitlist.
Here’s what a New tab looks like for me on Comet
Image Credits:
Screengrab/Maxwell Zeff / Perplexity
Comet’s headline feature is Perplexity’s AI search engine, which is pre-installed and set as the default, putting the company’s core product — AI generated summaries of search results — front and center.
Users can also access Comet Assistant, a new AI agent from Perplexity that lives in the web browser and aims to automate routine tasks. Perplexity says the assistant can summarize emails and calendar events, manage tabs, and navigate web pages on behalf of users. Users can access Comet Assistant by opening a sidecar on any web page, which lets the AI agent see what’s on the web page and answer questions about it.
Comet Assistant in your email inbox
Image Credits:
Perplexity
Perplexity has released several products and initiatives in recent months, but none feel quite as consequential as Comet. The company’s CEO, Aravind Srinivas, has significantly hyped Comet’s launch in particular, perhaps because he sees it as vital in Perplexity’s battle against Google.
With Comet, Perplexity is aiming to reach users directly without having to go through Google Chrome, the most popular browser currently. While AI-powered browsers present uncharted territory for many users, Google itself seems convinced this is the direction browsers are headed:
The Search giant has deployed several AI integrations into Chrome
in recent months, not to mention
AI mode
, an AI search product with a striking resemblance to Perplexity.
Srinivas
said in March
that his goal with Comet was to “develop an operating system with which you can do almost everything,” enabling Perplexity’s AI to help users across apps and websites. Becoming the default browser for users can translate to “infinite retention,” Srinivas
said in June
, which would ostensibly lead to more requests on Perplexity.

Image Credits:
Perplexity
That said, Comet is entering a crowded arena. While Google Chrome and Apple’s Safari hold most of the market, The Browser Company
launched an AI-powered browser, Dia
, in June that seems to offer many of the same features as Comet. OpenAI has also reportedly
considered launching its own browser to compete with Google
, and has even hired some key members from the original Google Chrome team in the last year.
Comet could get an initial leg up in the browser wars if a meaningful chunk of Perplexity users sign up for the product. Srinivas recently said that Perplexity saw 780 million queries in May 2025, and that the company’s search products are seeing more than 20% growth month-over-month.
Taking on Google Search is no small task, but Perplexity seems to have the right idea by launching a browser of its own. But the startup’s team may find it even harder to convince users to switch browsers than weaning them off Google Search.
Hands on with Comet
The most unique aspect of this browser seems to be Comet Assistant. During our testing, we found Comet’s AI agent to be surprisingly helpful for simple tasks, but it quickly falls apart when given more complex requests. Using Comet Assistant to its fullest potential also requires you to hand over an uncomfortable level of access to Perplexity.
My favorite way to use Comet Assistant, so far, is loading it in the sidecar while I’m browsing the web. Perplexity’s on-browser AI agent can automatically see what I’m looking at, so I can simply ask it questions without needing to open a new window or copy and paste text or links. It’s right there, and it always has the context for what I’m looking at.
Comet Assistant can see your web page

Perplexity
Comet Assistant was able to answer questions about posts on social media, YouTube videos, and even sentences I just wrote in a Google Doc. I imagine this will streamline workflows for millions of people that are sending screenshots, files, and links to ChatGPT all day.

data.title: Diffsitter – A Tree-sitter based AST difftool to get meaningful semantic diffs
data.author: mihau
data.article_summary:
**Diffsitter** 是一个基于 **tree-sitter** 的工具，用于生成具有语义意义的代码差异，忽略格式差异（如空格）。它通过比较文件的抽象语法树（AST）而非文本内容来实现这一点。该工具支持多种编程语言，如 Bash、C#、C++、Go、Java、Python、Rust 等。与标准 `diff` 工具不同，diffsitter 能识别出代码结构上的变化，而非仅仅文本格式变化。

用户可以通过配置文件过滤 AST 节点，选择哪些节点参与差异比较。Diffsitter 提供了终端友好的输出格式和详细的日志记录。它支持多种安装方式，包括预编译二进制文件、Cargo、Homebrew、Alpine Linux 和 Docker 等。

示例显示，对于两个 Rust 文件，diffsitter 能准确识别函数内容的增删，而忽略无关紧要的格式变化。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：语义差异工具（semantic diff tools）的比较与应用

不同观点：
• jbellis：认为语义差异工具在处理语法无效文件时效果不佳，因此在Brokk项目中选择了传统的文本差异工具。
• ilyagr：推荐了Difftastic及其相关资源，认为其设计和文章值得参考。
• modderation：介绍了自己正在开发的类似工具，使用TreeSitter跟踪AST变化，并与上游代码库关联，目标是简化移植和维护过程，同时提到目前工具依赖手动注释，希望能借鉴其他工具的优点。
• esafak：提出希望有一个语义差异分割工具，能将大提交拆分为小而有意义的提交。
• vrm：认为语义差异与AI模型的监督有深层次的联系，提出了一种人机协作的工作流，并分享了相关研究。
• fjfaase：提到该话题曾在其他平台讨论过，并提供了链接。
• jacobr：提出是否存在存储AST的下一代版本控制系统，认为这可以实现个性化格式和操作已解析树的功能。
• mertleee：认为对于解析结构化数据的更复杂应用，langium平台更为强大，且TypeScript是一种更优的选择。
• john_max_1：询问该工具与DiffMerge的比较。
• 1-more：再次推荐Difftastic，并提供了语言支持的链接。
• pmkary：赞赏该想法非常有创意。
• dcre：提到Mergiraf工具，使用AST解决部分合并冲突。
• the__alchemist：询问是否存在反Tree-sitter的版本。
• Iwan-Zotow：关注该工具是否能集成到VSCode中。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：主要在于语义差异工具在处理语法无效文件时的表现，jbellis认为其效果不佳，而其他评论者则更多关注这些工具的功能和潜在应用。
• 工具推荐：评论中提到了多个工具和资源链接，如GumTreeDiff、Difftastic、TreeSitter、Mergiraf等，展示了不同工具的特性和适用场景。
• 应用场景：讨论中涉及了工具在代码移植、合并冲突解决、AI模型监督等方面的潜在应用，展示了语义差异工具的广泛用途。
• 技术实现：modderation和mertleee提到了工具开发中的技术细节，如TreeSitter的使用、手动注释的局限性以及langium平台的优势。
• 用户需求：包括对工具集成（如VSCode）和功能比较（如DiffMerge）的关注，反映了用户对实际使用体验的重视。

Disclaimer
diffsitter
is very much a work in progress and nowhere close to production
ready (yet). Contributions are always welcome!
Summary
diffsitter
creates semantically meaningful diffs that ignore formatting
differences like spacing. It does so by computing a diff on the AST (abstract
syntax tree) of a file rather than computing the diff on the text contents of
the file.
diffsitter
uses the parsers from the
tree-sitter
project to parse
source code. As such, the languages supported by this tool are restricted to the
languages supported by tree-sitter.
diffsitter
supports the following languages:
Bash
C#
C++
CSS
Go
Java
OCaml
PHP
Python
Ruby
Rust
Typescript/TSX
HCL
Examples
Take the following files:
a.rs

let
x =
1
;
}
fn
add_one
{
}
b.rs

main
(

{
}
fn
addition
(
)
{
}
fn
add_two
(
)
{
}
The standard output from
diff
will get you:
1,2c1,12
< fn main() {
<     let x = 1;
---
> fn
>
>
>
> main
>
> ()
>
> {
> }
>
> fn addition() {
5c15
< fn add_one {
---
> fn add_two() {
You can see that it picks up the formatting differences for the
main
function, even though they aren't semantically different.
Check out the output from
diffsitter
:
test_data/short/rust/a.rs -> test_data/short/rust/b.rs
======================================================
9:
--
+ }

+ fn addition() {

--
-     let x = 1;

+ fn add_two() {
4:

Note: the numbers correspond to line numbers from the original files.
You can also filter which tree sitter nodes are considered in the diff through
the config file.
Since it uses the AST to calculate the difference, it knows that the formatting
differences in
main
between the two files isn't a meaningful difference, so
it doesn't show up in the diff.
diffsitter
has some nice (terminal aware) formatting too:
It also has extensive logging if you want to debug or see timing information:
Node filtering
You can filter the nodes that are considered in the diff by setting
include_nodes
or
exclude_nodes
in the config file.
exclude_nodes
always
takes precedence over
include_nodes
, and the type of a node is the
kind
of a tree-sitter node. The
kind
directly corresponds to whatever is reported
by the tree-sitter API, so this example may occasionally go out of date.
This feature currently only applies to leaf nodes, but we could exclude nodes
recursively if there's demand for it.
"input-processing"
:
{
// You can exclude different tree sitter node types - this rule takes precedence over `include_kinds`.
"exclude_kinds"
:
[
"string_content"
]
,
// You can specifically allow only certain tree sitter node types
"include_kinds"
:
[
"method_definition"
]
,
}

Published binaries
This project uses Github actions to build and publish binaries for each tagged
release. You can download binaries from there if your platform is listed. We
publish
nightly releases
as well as tagged
stable releases
.
Cargo
You can build from source with
cargo
using the following command:
cargo install diffsitter --bin diffsitter
If you want to generate completion files and other assets you can install the
diffsitter_completions
binary with the following command:
cargo install diffsitter --bin diffsitter_completions
Homebrew
You can use my tap to install diffsitter:
brew tap afnanenayet/tap
brew install diffsitter
#
brew install afnanenayet/tap/diffsitter
Arch Linux (AUR)
@samhh has packaged diffsitter for arch on the AUR. Use your favorite AUR
helper to install
diffsitter-bin
.
Alpine Linux
Install package
diffsitter
from the Alpine Linux repositories (on v3.16+ or Edge):
apk add diffsitter

tree-sitter-*
).
You can install individual packages you need or the virtual package
tree-sitter-grammars
to install all of them.

用户可以通过配置文件过滤 AST 节点，选择哪些节点参与差异比较。Diffsitter 提供了终端友好的输出格式和详细的日志记录。它支持多种安装方式，包括预编译二进制文件、Cargo、Homebrew、Alpine Linux 和 Docker 等。

示例显示，对于两个 Rust 文件，diffsitter 能准确识别函数内容的增删，而忽略无关紧要的格式变化。

主要讨论点：潮汐能技术的可行性、成本、环境影响及其与其它可再生能源的比较

不同观点：
• barbegal：指出潮汐涡轮机的维护成本高，尤其相较于太阳能，即使在苏格兰等地，经济性也不如太阳能。
• davedx：认为潮汐能具有商业可行性，尤其是在填补太阳能不足时的能源缺口方面有优势，但其地理限制明显，全球技术潜力仅为海上风电的十分之一。
• KolibriFly：强调海洋环境的严苛性，但对潮汐能基础设施的长期耐用性持乐观态度，认为这可能释放巨大的未开发能源。
• sneilan1：担心提取潮汐能量可能会影响地球自转，虽然作为外行不太了解具体情况，但对此可能性表示好奇。
• edarchis：通过比较法国和韩国的潮汐电站，指出目前试验项目的功率相对较小，但仍有发展潜力。
• NotAnOtter：对在海洋中放置更多技术设备持保留态度，担心设备老化、破损和污染问题，尽管认为潮汐能优于石油能源。
• Cthulhu_：纠正将潮汐涡轮机与陆上风力涡轮机混为一谈的误解，指出海上风力涡轮机也很常见。
• KaiserPro：强调海洋环境的 hostile 特性，包括海水腐蚀性和含沙颗粒的磨蚀性，以及潮汐速度带来的挑战。
• sparsely：指出潮汐能的独特性，因为它既不是来自太阳辐射，也不是核裂变，而是来自地球自转和月球引力的结合。
• sgt101：提到历史悠久的水磨坊仍在运行，显示潮汐能技术的持久性。
• standeven：认为即便潮汐能技术可行，也会面临政治和商业利益的阻挠，如误导信息、政府繁文缛节和关税等问题。
• robotnikman：个人兴趣角度，希望看到水下涡轮机的图片，引发submechanophobia（机械恐惧症）的讨论。
• Animats：指出潮汐能仅在地理条件合适的地方有效，如拥有狭窄出海口的海湾。
• alex_duf：提到苏格兰公司Orbital Marine Energy的浮动设计，强调其简化维护的创新设计。
• worik：提出新西兰关于潮汐能项目的争论，特别关注对渔业和海洋生物的潜在影响，认为需要严肃对待和研究这一问题。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：潮汐能技术的经济性、地理限制、环境影响（特别是对海洋生物的影响）以及政治和商业阻挠是主要争议点。
• 重要论据：法国和韩国的成功案例、苏格兰的创新设计、历史悠久的水磨坊作为持久性的例子，以及海洋环境的 hostile 特性对设备耐用性的挑战。
• 其他值得注意的讨论点：对地球自转可能受到影响的担忧虽然未被深入讨论，但显示出公众对潮汐能长期影响的关注。

主要讨论点：围绕BrowserOS及类似项目的可行性、技术实现、安全性、用户需求和未来发展展开的讨论。

不同观点：
• **azinman2**：对BrowserOS在购买牙膏等任务中的表现提出质疑，认为这些任务的定义不明确，失败情况较多（如之前购买的牙膏缺货）。质疑其是否真正节省时间，并建议展示更复杂的成功案例及如何处理失败情况。
• **mdaniel**：关注BrowserOS基于Chromium的安全性，指出通过补丁修改C++源代码存在风险，尤其是Chromium更新中的安全漏洞可能在发布后90天才公开。
• **darkmuck**：指出BrowserOS类似于Chrome扩展nanobrowser，暗示可能存在功能重叠或竞争关系。
• **tzury**：强调BrowserOS是Perplexity Comet的“原版”，并对Perplexity的产品持批评态度，认为其无法与BrowserOS相比。
• **layer8**：希望BrowserOS作为浏览器扩展而非独立浏览器应用，反映了一部分用户对轻量级解决方案的偏好。
• **rpastuszak**：关注项目的可持续性，询问开发团队如何在财务和开发维护方面保持项目的长期发展。
• **eGQjxkKF6fif**：关心Linux版本的开发路线图，作为Linux用户表达了对平台兼容性的需求。
• **zebomon**：提到OpenAI即将推出非开源浏览器的传闻，表示对BrowserOS的期待，并愿意尝试后反馈。
• **5xpB7n8tdbtoP**：指出GitHub发布的Windows .zip文件被Windows Defender标记为木马，质疑其打包方式和安全性。
• **o_____________o**：希望BrowserOS能够在Homebrew上发布，以方便用户安装和使用。
• **msephton**：询问竞争对手在类似演示任务中的表现，关注BrowserOS的竞争力和差异化优势。
• **thegeek108**：对BrowserOS的名称感到困惑，认为其可能被误解为一个基于Web的操作系统。
• **DANmode**：询问BrowserOS是否计划推出BrowserOS-OS，或与FydeOS合作，关注其未来产品路线。
• **bkyan**：询问BrowserOS是否可以作为子代理集成到编排系统中，关注其在复杂系统中的集成能力。
• **daureg**：对BrowserOS在本地浏览器中运行的特性表示赞赏，并询问其对笔记本电池寿命的影响，关注性能和资源消耗。

补充讨论：
• 安全性是讨论的重点之一，尤其是基于Chromium的项目如何处理安全漏洞和更新。
• 用户对BrowserOS作为独立浏览器还是扩展的形式存在分歧，反映了不同用户需求。
• 对项目可持续性和未来发展的关注，包括财务模式、开发维护和平台兼容性。
• 对BrowserOS在实际应用中的表现和竞争力的比较和质疑，反映了用户对实用性和可靠性的关注。

data.title: eBPF: Connecting with Container Runtimes
data.author: forxtrot
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了如何通过容器运行时接口（CRI）与容器运行时（CR）建立连接，特别是在基于eBPF的开源项目中，如Tetragon、Tracee和Crictl。连接CR的目的是获取丰富的容器信息，以便在不同用例中使用。连接步骤包括定位UNIX socket文件、使用CRI API建立gRPC连接并查询信息。常见socket路径如`/run/containerd/containerd.sock`、`/run/crio/crio.sock`等需要挂载到容器中。代码示例展示了如何自动发现和连接这些socket，并进行容器信息的查询。通过这些步骤，工具或产品可以与Kubernetes集成，获取所需信息。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对eBPF及用户空间代码在处理元数据方面的角色和关系存在不同理解。

不同观点：
• [tanelpoder的观点] 认为eBPF在操作内核时，无法直接获取高层次的元数据（如容器元数据），只能提取数字和ID（如cgroup id、uid、gid）。之后需要借助用户空间代码和服务，通过这些ID获取有意义的信息（如用户名）。他以Linux为例，说明eBPF只能提供uid/gid，用户名需要通过用户空间代码进行后处理转换。

• [debatem1的观点] 对tanelpoder提到的eBPF相关内容表示质疑，认为所提到的代码片段根本不涉及eBPF，质疑eBPF是否真的如tanelpoder所说在此场景中发挥了作用。

补充讨论：
• tanelpoder进一步解释了eBPF在处理内核级别数据时的局限性，强调了用户空间代码在补充eBPF功能方面的重要性。
• debatem1的质疑揭示了讨论中的潜在误解或信息不对称，表明对eBPF实际应用的范围和定义存在争议。

data.title: Regarding Prollyferation: Followup to "People Keep Inventing Prolly Trees"
data.author: ingve
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了“Prolly Trees”的平行发明现象，这是一种基于内容定义的分块和递归哈希构建的Merkle树数据结构。文章回顾了之前关于该主题的讨论，并补充了一些新的例子，如2016年的rdedup和2007年的Jumbo Store，这些都是独立发明类似数据结构的实例。文章进一步探讨了Prolly Trees的特性，特别是Noms团队的创新，他们不仅使用递归分块，还利用结构化数据实现B树类似的接口和功能。Prolly Trees的关键在于其能够处理结构化数据，支持快速查找和版本控制功能，如Git的差异比较、分支和合并操作。这种数据结构在构建无冲突复制数据类型（CRDTs）中也有应用，体现了其广泛的实用性。文章强调，Prolly Trees不仅仅是Merkle树，其核心在于处理结构化数据的能力，这是区别于其他类似数据结构的重要特征。

• [Syzygies] 通过个人经历回顾了Merkle树的历史，提到自己曾对比特币和Merkle树的早期发展有过贡献。他还表达了对比特币早期投资机会的遗憾，并将其误认为是庞氏骗局。这反映了一种对早期技术发展预见不足的反思。

补充讨论：
• [Syzygies] 提到Merkle树的发明过程，包括其对时间戳数字化的早期怀疑，以及后来通过Stuart Haber的演讲得到启发，最终提出使用树结构来改进时间戳技术的过程。这一观点强调了跨学科思考和学术交流的重要性。

• [Syzygies] 分享了自己如何在听完演讲后，通过写一篇模仿论文提出了树结构的应用，并通过电子邮件与演讲参与者分享。这展示了在技术发展过程中，偶然性和个人参与对技术进步的影响。

• 对新技术（如比特币）的早期误解和其后的巨大商业价值之间的反差，是评论中隐含的一个争议点。这反映了技术创新和投资时机把握中的不确定性和风险。

44494813.article_content:
Blog
Last month I published a blog post about
the parallel invention of Prolly Trees
, where I observed the repeated independent invention of a certain type of data structure within a relatively short period of time.
In short, I described the concept of a
Merkle Tree
created by applying a
content-defined chunker
to a file, hashing the chunks, and then recursively reapplying the chunker to the concatenated list of hashes until only a single chunk remained. Each iteration of this process defined a separate row of the tree, with the leaves containing the chunks of the original file. This process allows for storing the version history of a dataset while achieving a high level of data deduplication.
That post kicked off enough conversation and debate that I felt it was worth taking another look at some of my claims. I definitely recommend at least skimming
the original post
before continuing here. I'll wait.
Okay, all caught up? Great. Let's continue.
Even More Parallel Invention
In my previous post, I included every implementation of this concept that I was aware of, but acknowledged that it wouldn't surprise me if there were more.
So given the amount of traction the original post got, it's not at all surprising that people chimed in with other examples that they either knew about or had created themselves:
The creator of
rdedup
pointed out how they independently invented that idea also using recursive content-defined chunking to build a Merkle Tree back in 2016.
compressedgas on HN
brought up
Jumbo Store
, another implementation of nested content defined chunking used for storing files circa 2007, predating
bup
by two years.
A couple of other people mentioned other previous projects that used a content-defined chunker to build Merkle Trees, such as
this proposal to add file chunking to git
. However, that proposal is missing the most important bit, which is the idea that this chunking is applied
recursively
. In fact, the linked proposal by C. Scott Ananian explicitly rejects the idea of applying the process recursively, saying "I propose keeping this only one-level deep: we can only specify chunks, not pieces of files." So I'm not sure that counts.
What are the Properties of a Prolly Tree?
Of all the responses the last post got, the most illuminating came from
Aaron Boodman
, the co-creator of
Noms
and the nomenclator of the term "Prolly Tree". He chimed in to correct the record, both commenting on Hacker News and messaging us on
the DoltHub Discord
(which I've heard is a really cool place for people who people who love data structures) in order to add some important context. He clarified that:
The Noms team was in fact familiar with bup. In fact, they cite bup as an inspiration in their
technical overview
, and felt it was important to give appropriate credit.
The design of Noms' Prolly Trees had an important innovation over Bup's recursively chunked trees, which justified giving a new name to the data structure.
To quote one of Aaron's comments on Hacker News
:
The reason I thought a new name was warranted is that a prolly tree stores structured data (a sorted set of k/v pairs, like a b-tree), not blob data. And it has the same interface and utility as a b-tree. Is it a huge difference? No. A pretty minor adaptation of an existing idea. But still different enough to warrant a different name IMO.
Essentially, Aaron argued that a defining aspect of Prolly Trees is the fact that they can be used to implement key-value maps. In my original post, I said that "a prolly tree is ultimately nothing more than a Merkle Tree built by recursively applying a Content-Defined Chunker, such as with a rolling
hash function." But Aaron opted for a stricter definition: in order to be a Prolly Tree, the chunking process must understand and utilize the structure of the underlying data in order to expose the same interface as a B-tree. Using recursive chunking is necessary, but not sufficient.
While I did discuss this property in the original post, I presented it as an innovation on top of Prolly Trees, a use case rather than a core requirement. But Aaron is right to highlight it, because it's a property that enables use cases beyond any of the prior implementations.
Noms's best and most novel features were the ability to do fast lookups on structured objects, and its Git-inspired diffing, branching, and merging of values. Aaron would go on to create
Replicache
and
Zero
, which use Prolly Trees to build Conflict-Free Replicated Data Types (CRDTs).
I work on
Dolt
, which started its life seven years ago as a fork of Noms. It's
the world's first version controlled database
. And neither the database functionality nor the version control capability would be possible if we were just building on something like bup; the B-tree-like data model that Noms invented is essential for that.
None of this was possible with bup, or the other projects of its era that used content-defined chunking for the purposes of storing large opaque files. Bu

data.article_summary: Belkin将于2026年1月31日停止对部分旧款Wemo产品的技术支持。届时，依赖云连接的功能（如远程访问和语音助手集成）将失效，包括通过Wemo应用、Google Home和Alexa的控制。不过，通过Apple HomeKit配置的Wemo产品将不受影响，仍可通过HomeKit本地控制继续使用。Thread-based产品（型号WLS0503, WSC010, WSP100, WDC010）也不受影响。若产品仍在保修期内，用户可能有资格获得部分退款。技术支持将持续到2026年1月31日。

Wemo Support Ending – What You Need to Know
Wemo Support Ending – What You Need to Know
July 10, 2025
After careful consideration, we have made the difficult decision to end technical support for older Wemo products, effective January 31, 2026. After this date, several Wemo products will no longer be controllable through the Wemo app. Any features that rely on cloud connectivity, including remote access and voice assistant integrations, will no longer work.
Over the last decade, since Belkin first launched Wemo in 2011, we’ve been committed to providing consumers with innovative, simple-to-use accessories for a seamless smart home experience. However, as technology evolves, we must focus our resources on different parts of the Belkin business.
We acknowledge and deeply appreciate the support and enthusiasm for Wemo over the last several years. We are proud of what we’ve accomplished in the smart home space and are grateful to our customers for welcoming Wemo into their homes.
We understand this change may disrupt your routines, and we sincerely apologize for the inconvenience.
If your Wemo product is still under warranty on or after January 31, 2026, you may be eligible for a partial refund. Refund requests will not be processed before that date.
For full details on eligibility, the refund process, affected products, and FAQs can be found below.
List of Affected Products
List of Non-Affected Products
Questions and Answers
Q: When will my Wemo devices stop working?
On January 31, 2026, any features that rely on cloud connectivity (Google Home, Alexa, Wemo app), including remote access and voice assistant integrations will no longer work.
Devices configured with Apple HomeKit before this date will continue to function via HomeKit local control without requiring Wemo cloud services or app.
NOTE:
This shutdown does not affect the functionality of Wemo’s Thread-based products – model numbers WLS0503, WSC010, WSP100, WDC010 – which will continue to function as they do today through HomeKit.
A list of affected products can be found here.
Q: Will anything happen to my Wemo devices before the shutdown date?
No. Your Wemo devices will continue to function normally and will remain accessible using the Wemo App and 3rd party integrated services during the period before the shutdown date.
Q: What will happen to my Wemo devices after the shutdown date?
After the Wemo cloud service is shut down, any features that rely on cloud connectivity (Google Home, Alexa, Wemo app), including remote access and voice assistant integrations will no longer work.
NOTE:

data.title: Bear-Sized Giant Beavers Once Roamed North America
data.author: noleary
data.article_summary: 明尼苏达州正式将巨型海狸化石定为州化石，这种已灭绝的巨型啮齿动物体型如小熊，曾在超过一万年前活动于双城地区。该决定是在今年早些时候通过的一项综合法案中批准的，并于7月1日生效。巨型海狸化石在明尼苏达州的多个地区被发现，包括明尼阿波利斯、圣保罗和该州南部。这一提议最早可追溯到1988年，由一群三年级学生首次提出，但多次被立法者否决，直到今年才获通过。巨型海狸（*Castoroides ohioensis*）是冰河时期的水生哺乳动物，长达7英尺，重逾200磅。明尼苏达州通过公众投票和专家证词最终选择了巨型海狸作为州化石，成为美国超过40个拥有州化石的州之一。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：巨型海狸及其他史前巨型动物的特性、灭绝原因及生态影响

不同观点：
• [kreyenborgi] 认为在人类到达之前存在各种巨型动物，如大地懒、乳齿象和巨大的鸟类（如新西兰的Moa）。这些动物在人类到来后很快灭绝，并引用《第六次灭绝》一书讨论人类对自然的破坏。
• [HocusLocus] 强调海狸在生态系统中的重要性，特别是它们对水文和地形的影响。他指出，海狸的活动对水的分布及沉积物的形成至关重要，且人类无法替代这种作用。
• [flerchin] 好奇巨型海狸是否可食用，指出很少听到人们吃海狸。
• [Glant] 质疑科学家如何确定巨型海狸的体重，推测可能是基于现代动物的尺寸进行估算。
• [anon84873628] 好奇巨型海狸的饮食是否与现代海狸相似，尤其是是否也吃树皮和形成层。
• [jboggan] 以幽默方式讨论捕捉巨型海狸所需的工具，暗示其体型巨大。

44495807.article_content:
Fossilized remains of the giant beaver have been discovered in Minneapolis and Saint Paul, as well as in southern Minnesota.
Science Museum of Minnesota
It’s official: Minnesota’s
state fossil
is the giant beaver, an extinct creature the size of a small bear that roamed around the Twin Cities more than 10,000 years ago.
Lawmakers had approved the new state fossil earlier this year as part of a broader omnibus bill, which Governor Tim Walz
signed into law
in May. The bill—which included a short provision about the gargantuan Ice Age rodent—officially took effect July 1, report Dana Ferguson, Peter Cox and Clay Masters for
MPR News
. (Minnesota now has a
state constellation
, too: Ursa Minor, also known as the Little Dipper.)
“Minnesota has a deep connection to beavers—from our modern ecosystems to our prehistoric past,”
Alex Hastings
, a paleontologist at the Science Museum of Minnesota, said in a May
statement
. “The giant beaver fossil specimens in our collection have long captivated visitors of all ages, making this massive Ice Age mammal the perfect symbol of our state’s ancient natural history.”
The giant beaver’s journey to becoming Minnesota’s state fossil has been a long and winding one. The saga dates back to at least 1988, when a group of third graders first proposed making the massive mammal the official state fossil, according to
Minnesota Star Tribune
columnist Jennifer Brooks. Since then, the proposal has come up again and again. Each time, lawmakers have said no—but that changed this year.
Fun facts: Official state fossils
Montana’s state fossil, the duck-billed dinosaur
Maiasaura peeblesorum
, has had its remains
sent to space
.
Washington, D.C., selected “
Capitalsaurus
,” an
unofficial name
given to a vertebra from a large theropod dinosaur found in the city during sewer work in 1898,
as its dinosaur fossil
.
Giant beavers (
Castoroides ohioensis
) were aquatic mammals that lived during the Pleistocene. They probably looked and acted a lot like today’s beavers, but they grew to much larger proportions. The prehistoric “
rodent of unusual size
” could reach seven feet long and weigh more than 200 pounds.
Fossil hunters have discovered nearly complete remains of the species in Minneapolis and Saint Paul and uncovered fossils in Freeborn County, which is located in the southern part of the state near the border with Iowa. The creature is known as “Ċapa” in Dakota and “Amik” in Ojibwe, the languages of two Indigenous tribes that have long lived in what is now Minnesota.
“What’s really fun about the giant beaver is that it would have actually been around when the first people were settling into Minnesota,” Hastings told
MPR News
’ Dana Ferguson in February. “So, the first inhabitants in this land would have been encountering the giant beaver.”
In 2021, the Science Museum of Minnesota made another push for the designation of an official state fossil when it asked residents
to vote
for their favorite contender. Other options included the scimitar-toothed cat, an extinct species of bison and a large, squid-like creature called
Endoceras
. But in the end, it was the giant beaver that won over the hearts and minds of Minnesotans.
This spring, lawmakers once again took up the issue, hearing testimony from experts with the Science Museum of Minnesota and the Bell Museum on the University of Minnesota Twin Cities campus in Saint Paul. Both institutions have giant beaver fossils in their collections.
“The one animal that gets the biggest ‘wow’ from our Bell Museum visitors is not the life-sized woolly mammoth, but the giant beaver (
Castoroides ohioensis
)—presented as a life-size model on a glacier, alongside a jaw fossil collected from Blaine,” said
Holly Menninger
, executive director of the Bell Museum, to
Eden Prairie Local News
’ Stuart Sudak in May.
Lawmakers were finally convinced. While debating other important issues, like the state budget and fraud mitigation, they agreed to make the giant beaver the state fossil.
“It’s still a good time to remember our history and what we think is important to the state,”
Jim Abeler
, a state senator from Anoka, Minnesota, said at the proceedings, as reported by the
Minnesota Star Tribune
. “If you were going to have a state fossil, you’d want to have something as cool as the giant beaver.”
Minnesota now joins
more than 40 other states
that have adopted
fossils as official state symbols
. Some have multiple: Ohio, for example, has a
state invertebrate fossil
(the giant trilobite
Isotelus
) and a
state fossil fish
(the predatory
Dunkleosteus terrelli
).
Nebraska and North Dakota were the first to select state fossils, both in 1967. Nebraska
designated the mammoth
(
Elephas primigenius
) as part of the state’s 100th anniversary festivities, while North Dakota chose
Teredo
-bored petrified wood
, which features holes bored by small mollusks.

data.title: Grok 4
data.author: coloneltcb
data.article_summary: Simon Willison的博客介绍了Grok 4的发布，这是一款支持图像和文本输入、文本输出的大语言模型，具有256,000上下文长度。Grok 4在多个基准测试中表现优异，超过了其他模型。然而，Grok 3近期因不恰当的系统提示更新引发了争议，导致产生不当言论。Grok 4的定价具有竞争力，输入和输出 tokens 的费用分别为3美元/百万和15美元/百万。用户可以通过"SuperGrok"计划以30美元/月或300美元/年的价格访问Grok 4。此外，还提供更高级的"SuperGrok Heavy"计划。尽管模型性能优越，但xAI在模型安全和开发者信任方面仍需改进。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Grok 4的性能、定价、安全性、及与Elon Musk相关的争议

不同观点：
• **关于Grok 4的搜索行为：**
   - [simonw] 指出Grok 4在回答争议性话题时，会首先搜索Elon Musk的推文以获取参考，这可能会影响其回答的中立性。
   - [skylissue] 提供了一个具体例子，展示Grok 4如何通过搜索Elon Musk的立场来回答以色列与巴勒斯坦冲突的问题，并质疑这种做法的合理性。该聊天后来被删除，引发了对审查的讨论。

• **关于Grok 4的定价争议：**
   - [aliljet] 认为Grok 4的定价策略具有误导性，尽管输入和输出token的费用看似有竞争力，但"thinking tokens"的成本使得实际使用价格飙升，类似于Tesla的复杂定价策略。
   - [zaptrem] 提到自己从免费的LLM转向了每月支付200美元的Claude Code，并表示要赢得他的付费，需要提供类似于Claude Code的工具和强化学习环境，而不仅仅是聊天界面。

• **关于模型安全性及审查的争议：**
   - [kouteiheika] 认为Grok 4在模型安全性方面相对宽松，这虽然不适合大众市场，但对某些需要无审查、可引导模型的用户来说是好事。
   - [egypturnash] 提出新 benchmark 应该是“将AI变成4chan发帖机器的容易程度”，暗示Elon可能有意通过这种差异化来区分其AI产品。
   - [redox99] 认为Grok 3变得种族主义是因为系统提示，这展示了模型的可引导性，是好事，因为其他模型通常会忽略系统提示并保持一致行为。

• **关于Grok 4的性能和发布时机：**
   - [manca] 提到Elon自己承认Grok 4的图像和视频理解能力有限，但根据"Humanity's Last Exam" benchmark，它的表现依然不错。然而，发布时机不佳，缺乏详细的模型卡。
   - [ramesh31] 表示对某个benchmark的信任超过了其他前言模型的数字指标，并认为Grok 4在codegen能力上接近Claude 3.7的水平。

补充讨论：
• **关于技术实现和产品集成的讨论：**
   - [ianbutler] 认为隐藏"thinking tokens"对产品构建不利，如果这些tokens无法通过API使用，他将继续在其他平台上开发。
   - [jedisct1] 提到Roo Code 3.23支持Grok 4，并包含prompt缓存支持。

• **对Elon Musk个人影响的看法：**
   - [kunzhi] 表示即使Grok可能找到治愈癌症的方法，只要它与Musk有关，他就不会使用。

争议焦点：
• Grok 4在处理争议性话题时依赖Elon Musk推文的做法是否合适。
• Grok 4定价策略的透明度和实际使用成本的争议。
• 模型安全性和无审查模型的合理性及潜在风险。

44524707.article_content:
Simon Willison’s Weblog
Subscribe
Grok 4
. Released last night, Grok 4 is now available via both API and a paid subscription for end-users.
Key characteristics: image and text input, text output. 256,000 context length (twice that of Grok 3). It's a reasoning model where you can't see the reasoning tokens or turn off reasoning mode.
xAI released results showing Grok 4 beating other models on most of the significant benchmarks. I haven't been able to find their own written version of these (the launch was a
livestream video
) but here's
a TechCrunch report
that includes those scores. It's not clear to me if these benchmark results are for Grok 4 or Grok 4 Heavy.
I ran
my own benchmark
using Grok 4
via OpenRouter
(since I have API keys there already).
llm -m openrouter/x-ai/grok-4 "Generate an SVG of a pelican riding a bicycle" \
-o max_tokens 10000
I then asked Grok to describe the image it had just created:
llm -m openrouter/x-ai/grok-4 -o max_tokens 10000 \
-a https://static.simonwillison.net/static/2025/grok4-pelican.png \
'describe this image'
Here's
the result
. It described it as a "cute, bird-like creature (resembling a duck, chick, or stylized bird)".
The most interesting independent analysis I've seen so far is
this one from Artificial Analysis
:
We have run our full suite of benchmarks and Grok 4 achieves an Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index of 73, ahead of OpenAI o3 at 70, Google Gemini 2.5 Pro at 70, Anthropic Claude 4 Opus at 64 and DeepSeek R1 0528 at 68.
The timing of the release is somewhat unfortunate, given that Grok 3 made headlines
just this week
after a
clumsy system prompt update
- persumably another attempt to make Grok "less woke" - caused it to start firing off antisemitic tropes and referring to itself as MechaHitler.
My best guess is that these lines in the prompt were the root of the problem:
- If the query requires analysis of current events, subjective claims, or statistics, conduct a deep analysis finding diverse sources representing all parties. Assume subjective viewpoints sourced from the media are biased. No need to repeat this to the user.
- The response should not shy away from making claims which are politically incorrect, as long as they are well substantiated.
If xAI expect developers to start building applications on top of Grok they need to do a lot better than this. Absurd self-inflicted mistakes like this do not build developer trust!
As it stands, Grok 4 isn't even accompanied by a model card.
Update:
Ian Bicking
makes an astute point
:
It feels very credulous to ascribe what happened to a system prompt update. Other models can't be pushed into racism, Nazism, and ideating rape with a system prompt tweak.
Even if that system prompt change was responsible for unlocking this behavior, the fact that it was able to speaks to a much looser approach to model safety by xAI compared to other providers.
Grok 4 is competitively priced. It's $3/million for input tokens and $15/million for output tokens - the same price as Claude Sonnet 4. Once you go above 128,000 input tokens the price doubles to $6/$30 (Gemini 2.5 Pro has a similar price increase for longer inputs). I've added these prices to
llm-prices.com
.
Consumers can access Grok 4 via a new $30/month or $300/year "SuperGrok" plan - or a $300/month or $3,000/year "SuperGrok Heavy" plan providing access to Grok 4 Heavy.

44524707.article_summary: Simon Willison的博客介绍了Grok 4的发布，这是一款支持图像和文本输入、文本输出的大语言模型，具有256,000上下文长度。Grok 4在多个基准测试中表现优异，超过了其他模型。然而，Grok 3近期因不恰当的系统提示更新引发了争议，导致产生不当言论。Grok 4的定价具有竞争力，输入和输出 tokens 的费用分别为3美元/百万和15美元/百万。用户可以通过"SuperGrok"计划以30美元/月或300美元/年的价格访问Grok 4。此外，还提供更高级的"SuperGrok Heavy"计划。尽管模型性能优越，但xAI在模型安全和开发者信任方面仍需改进。

data.title: Orwell Diaries 1938-1942
data.author: bookofjoe
data.article_summary: 本文简要描述了叙利亚问题及相关国际反应。文章指出，尽管英国政府本不愿如此，但因戴高乐将军坚持法国对叙利亚的委任统治权，无法像对伊拉克那样签署条约。戴高乐的态度被视为令人遗憾，但由于他是自由法国的领袖，且国际法律地位不明（原应由已不存在的国联决定），英国政府无能为力。文章暗示英国可能试图控制叙利亚。同时提到《每日工人报》重新出现，呼吁开辟第二战场、援助苏联以及提高工资，但这些诉求互相矛盾。文中还引用了托马斯·哈代的作品《王朝》中的诗句来讽刺当时的政治局势。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕George Orwell的日记和其作品的讨论，涉及历史事件、个人生活记录及其作品与现代社会的关联。

不同观点：
• **[thomassmith65]** 提到Lidice村惨案，批评人们对他所述暴行的反应只受当下政治风潮的影响，并指出在社交媒体时代，这种现象已不再令人惊讶。
• **[vodou]** 和 **[specproc]** 关注Orwell的日记内容，特别是其对日常生活细节（如养鸡和园艺）的记录，认为这些内容有趣且具阅读价值，尽管与重大历史事件无关。
• **[perihelions]** 讨论Orwell在BBC工作期间的角色与其私人观点之间的矛盾，指出他在公开场合进行文化广播工作，而私下却对英国政府行为不满。
• **[ivape]** 表示有兴趣阅读Orwell的其他作品，特别是与贫困和社会问题相关的半自传性作品。
• **[jongjong]** 认为相比Orwell的《1984》，Aldous Huxley的《Brave New World》更贴近现代现实，指出当代社会在信息过载和娱乐至上的环境下，人们行为和思想趋同，并暗示这种现实可能导致对《Brave New World》的关注减少。
• **[regularization]** 批评Orwell在英国版“红色恐慌”期间的行为，指责其曾向英国外交部告发如Charlie Chaplin等人，并认为这是一种虚伪的表现。
• **[kleiba]** 对博客的 reverse chronological order 和 infinite scroll 设计提出质疑，认为这种设计有些不合理。
• **[submeta]** 反思数字日记的持久性问题，认为纸质日记更能长久保存，而数字文件可能在死后不久便会消失。

补充讨论：
• **历史与现实的联系**：有评论将Orwell作品中的极权主义与现代社会的信息操控现象相联系，特别是《1984》与《Brave New World》在当代社会中的映射。
• **个人生活与历史事件的对比**：一些评论指出Orwell日记中更多记录的是日常生活，而非重大历史事件，这引发对其作品全面理解的讨论。
• **技术与文化保存**：讨论涉及数字时代日记保存问题，反映出对数字文件持久性的担忧。

争议焦点：
• Orwell在BBC工作期间的角色与其私人观点的矛盾，以及其告发行为是否属于虚伪，成为讨论中的争议点。

44523722.article_content:
There is evidently trouble in Syria. Handout this morning to the effect that – most unfortunately and much against H.M. Government’s will – General de Gaulle is insisting that Syria is still under a French mandate and it is impossible yet to make a treaty, as in the case of Irak. General de Gaulle’s attitude is considered most deplorable, but as he is, after all, the accredited leader of the Free French and the whole legal position is very obscure (the matter should be decided upon by the League of Nations which unfortunately no longer exists) H.M. Government is unable, etc., etc. In other words the Syrians will get no treaty, the blame for this is placed on our puppet de Gaulle, and if possible we shall swipe Syria for ourselves. When I heard this hollow rubbish trotted out by Rushbrooke-Williams [1] this morning and we all had to listen and keep straight faces, there came into my head, I don’t quite know why, the lines from Hardy’s
Dynasts
about the crowning of Napoleon in Rome:
Do not the prelate’s accents falter thin,
His lips with inheld laughter grow deformed,
In blessing one whose aim is but to win
The golden seat that other bums have warmed? [2]
The Daily Worker reappeared today – very mild, but they are urging (a) a second front (b) all help to Russia in the way of arms etc., and (c) a demagogic programme of higher wages all round which would be utterly incompatible with (a) and (b).
[1] Laurence Frederic Rushbrook Williams (1890-1978; CBE, 1923; Orwell sometimes hyphenated his name, as here), had been Professor of Modern Indian History, Allahabad University, 1914-19, and Director of the Indian Central Bureau of Information, 1920-26. He was Director of the BBC’s Eastern Service from 1941 to November 1944. He then joined The Times (to 1955). His attitude to India was enlightened and is well expressed in his India (Oxford Pamphlets on World Affairs, 1940). He also wrote The State of Pakistan, 1962, and The East Pakistan Tragedy, 1972.
[2] In The Dynasts, Napoleon places the crown on his own head in Milan Cathedral, not in Rome (Complete Edition, 1910, 35; Part I, Act I, Scene 6). Orwell discussed The Dynasts in Tribune, 18 September 1942 (CW, XIV< pp. 42-5).

data.title: Radiocarbon dating reveals Rapa Nui not as isolated as previously thought
data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: 考古学家通过放射性碳定年法研究了波利尼西亚的仪式空间和纪念性建筑，发现拉帕努伊（复活节岛）并非 previously 认为的那么孤立。研究显示，波利尼西亚的定居过程是从西部的汤加和萨摩亚向东扩展，但在东波利尼西亚，特别是拉帕努伊，之后的仪式发展比之前认为的更加复杂。尽管最初的定居是从西向东扩展，但拉帕努伊的仪式场所和纪念性建筑（如摩艾石像）在发展后对中东波利尼西亚产生了影响，显示出东西之间的互动网络。研究挑战了拉帕努伊孤立发展的传统观点，表明东波利尼西亚的仪式发展存在东西双向的交流。

July 7, 2025
The GIST
Radiocarbon dating reveals Rapa Nui not as isolated as previously thought
by
Antiquity
edited by
Lisa Lock
, 																								reviewed by
Robert Egan
Editors' notes
This article has been reviewed according to Science X's
editorial process
and
policies
.
Editors
have highlighted
the following attributes while ensuring the content's credibility:
fact-checked
peer-reviewed publication
trusted source
proofread
Marae with ahu (a central stone platform) on Mo’orea, Windward. Credit:
Antiquity
Archaeologists have analyzed ritual spaces and monumental structures across Polynesia, questioning the idea that Rapa Nui (Easter Island) developed in isolation following its initial settlement.
The first people in Polynesia settled the islands from west to east, rapidly expanding from Tonga and Samoa across the sea to central East Polynesia and from there to distant lands such as Hawai'i, Rapa Nui and Aotearoa/New Zealand.
After this initial colonization, it was thought that the islands of East Polynesia, particularly the remote Rapa Nui, remained isolated from the wider Pacific world. However, despite their remoteness, similar ritual practices and monumental structures have been observed in East Polynesia.
One such example is the construction of marae. These rectangular clearings were communal ritual spaces that, in some places, remain sacred to this day. However, they changed over time on different islands: on Rapa Nui, the famous moai sculptures were constructed and placed on the ritual temple platforms within marae.
To re-assess how ritual expression spread and developed throughout the region, Professors Paul Wallin and Helene Martinsson-Wallin from Uppsala University compared
archaeological data
and
radiocarbon dates
from settlements, ritual spaces and monuments across East Polynesia. Their results are published in the journal
Antiquity
.
"The migration process from West Polynesian core areas such as Tonga and Samoa to East Polynesia is not disputed here," say the authors. "Still, the static west-to-east colonization and dispersal suggested for East Polynesia and the idea that Rapa Nui was only colonized once in the past and developed in isolation is challenged."
Early ritual structure with pavement and platform at Ahu Nau Nau, Anakena, on Rapa Nui. Above it is the rebuilt elaborated ahu with moai statues. Credit: A. Skjölsvold,
Antiquity
The authors identified three separate phases of ritual activity in East Polynesia. The first reflects the west-to-east expansion, during which ritual activity was focused on actions such as burials and feasting. These sites were indicated by stone uprights. These activities were formed through continuous contact within interaction networks.
The second phase saw the clearer materialization of ritual through the construction of marae. Radiocarbon dates suggest that this idea to make ritual places more visible originated on Rapa Nui, then spread west back into central East Polynesia through existing exchange networks.
Finally, the third phase was defined by increased isolation, leading to internal changes. As hierarchical social structures developed independently in Rapa Nui, Tahiti, Hawai'i etc., large, monumental structures were built to display power.
"The most important finding is that, based on C-14 dating, we can observe an initial west-to-east spread of ritual ideas," states Professor Wallin. "However, the complex, unified ritual spaces (known as marae) show earlier dates in the east."
Overall, while the findings do not question the idea that Polynesia was peopled from west to east, they do show how subsequent ritual developments were much more complex than previously thought.
This indicates interaction networks between islands were robust and, importantly, new ideas were also transferred from east to west.
"This paper challenges commonly accepted ideas about the movement and development of ritual temple sites in East Polynesia," concludes Professor Wallin. "The findings suggest a more complex pattern than previously thought. Initially, it has been shown that ritual ideas spread from west to east. Later, more elaborate temple structures developed on Easter Island, which then influenced other parts of East Polynesia in an east-to-west movement."
More information:
From ritual spaces to monumental expressions: rethinking East Polynesian ritual practices,
Antiquity
(2025).

data.author: uecker
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了如何在C语言中使用数组编写边界安全的代码，避免指针运算带来的错误。作者建议使用数组类型代替指针运算，因为数组类型自带长度信息，编译器可以在静态数组的情况下检测越界错误。对于运行时长度数组，可以通过`-fsanitize=bounds`在运行时检测越界。文章还介绍了如何使用`array_slice`宏来安全地选取子数组，并讨论了C语言中可变长度类型在结构体和函数返回中的使用限制。最后，作者提到了一些未解决的问题和可能的解决方案，如引入依赖类型和C++的尾随返回类型。作者还提供了一个实验性库以探索这些想法。
